subject.title: fix(slack): bound one-shot WebClient/write timeouts without Bolt deadline

question: Should existing Slack users receive unconditional 30-second one-shot web and 60-second write deadlines, including users behind slow proxies or performing large uploads?
rationale: The patch fixes a real unbounded-hang path, but selecting unconditional request deadlines is an upgrade-sensitive reliability tradeoff that source inspection and stalled-request proof cannot settle alone.

options.title: Confirm defaults with upgrade proof
options.body: Retain the proposed values after demonstrating a representative slow-success or upload path and recording the acceptable compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Narrow the first change
options.body: Land the lower-risk one-shot web deadline now and defer the write deadline until upload and ambiguous-write behavior has stronger proof.

options.title: Accept the bounded-failure tradeoff
options.body: Land both defaults as written and explicitly accept that slow existing requests may now fail rather than wait indefinitely.

recommendation.title: Confirm defaults with upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Retain the proposed values after demonstrating a representative slow-success or upload path and recording the acceptable compatibility tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merge history connects this person to the affected Slack client-option boundary and its integration behavior.
